head_commit.message:
chore: move codex-exec unit tests into sibling files (#16581)

## Why

`codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs` already keeps unit tests in a sibling
`lib_tests.rs` module so the implementation stays top-heavy and easier
to read. This applies that same layout to the rest of
`codex-rs/exec/src` so each production file keeps its entry points and
helpers ahead of test code.

## What

- Move inline unit tests out of `cli.rs`, `main.rs`,
`event_processor_with_human_output.rs`, and
`event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs` into sibling `*_tests.rs` files.
- Keep test modules wired through `#[cfg(test)]` plus `#[path = "..."]
mod tests;`, matching the `lib.rs` pattern.
- Preserve the existing test coverage and assertions while making this a
source-layout-only refactor.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p codex-exec`

head_commit.message:
fix(tui): treat non-ASCII characters as individual word units in word movement

Option/Alt+Arrow word navigation previously treated entire CJK (Chinese,
Japanese, Korean) sequences as a single word because the word-boundary
logic only recognised a hardcoded set of ASCII punctuation separators.
Characters outside that set — including all CJK codepoints — were
grouped together, causing the cursor to jump over full runs of CJK text
in one keystroke.

Fix: in both `beginning_of_previous_word` and `end_of_next_word`, treat
any non-ASCII character as its own word unit. A non-ASCII anchor char
stops movement immediately; a non-ASCII char encountered while scanning
an ASCII word also terminates the scan.

Add three regression tests that cover pure-CJK backward/forward movement
and mixed ASCII+CJK text in both directions.

Fixes #16584
